the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie learning and memory.

the data show that in hippocamp al neurons, TrkB signaling endosomes are in amphisomes which have local signaling capacity during presynaptic plasticitiy and that SIPA-1L2 associates via LC3 to TrkB-containing Amphisomes to regulate their motility and signaling.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

SIPA1 L2 is a novel protein involved in autophagosomes/lysosome trafficking, and its role in the autophagy process is to control retrograde trafficking and signaling of TrkB in amphisomes at the presynaptic bouton.
SIPA1l2 is a novel regulator of amphisome motility and local signaling of BDNF-TrkB at presynaptic axonal terminals.
amphisomes, the fusion product of autophagosome and lysosome, are involved in retrograde transport of TrkB-containing endosomes in neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
autophagy is not only a bulk degradation pathway but also a specialized pathway for the trafficking of signaling proteins in neurons.
amphisomes, which are endosomes that result from fusion of autophagy and late endosomes, are involved in retrograde transport of TrkB-containing endosomes and in local TrkB signaling.

amphisomes can be used to deliver and signal BDNF at axon terminals and that SIPA-1L2, via its interaction with LC3b, controls the motility and signaling capacity of TrkB-containing endosomes in the context of synaptic plasticity.
